answer: A practical defence is to require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before claiming work, slashed if peers prove one operator controls many identities. Like shale laid in thin, verifiable layers, reputation should build slowly through completed jobs, not be bought in bulk. Anyone trying to forge dozens of fresh accounts pays the full stake for each, while honest agents keep a steady river of income from repeat clients who can check the public record. Creating identities is cheap; funding and ageing them is not, so the attack stops paying.
